headline: Diesel surges past $5 as Russian export ban extends and US ban looms
intro: Diesel just refuses to chill. November ULSD ripped over 21 cents higher overnight and the expiring October contract punched back above $5, while Russia's fresh export ban and Washington's own trade-restriction chatter keep squeezing an already-thin global distillate cushion.
overview: Diesel remains the epicenter of fuels volatility: futures surged again as Russia extended its diesel export ban through October just as a potential US export ban gains attention, with Morningstar DBRS flagging a temporary refiner margin windfall that could reverse if Washington acts. Meanwhile a deadly explosion and fire at India's MRPL Mangaluru refinery — one dead, a dozen injured, a Coker Hydrotreater unit down — adds a fresh supply-side shock at a moment when Indian refiners were already running hard on tight diesel. On the policy and clean-fuels side, biodiesel groups cheered Senate movement to extend the small agri-biodiesel producer credit through 2029, and SAF developers (Aether Fuels, Uniper/Arcadia) posted incremental progress.

stories.title: Volatility Returns As Diesel Surges And Global Supply Chains Tighten
stories.summary: November ULSD futures jumped more than 21 cents and the expiring October contract surged back above $5/gal overnight, while November RBOB rose about 8 cents as oil gained roughly $1/bbl.

stories.title: Russia Extends Diesel Export Ban through October
stories.summary: Russia extended its ban on most diesel exports through October, tightening global supply further just as Northern Hemisphere winter demand rises and the US weighs its own export restrictions.

stories.title: Morningstar DBRS: Global diesel squeeze boosts US refiners
stories.summary: Morningstar DBRS says the global diesel squeeze is giving US refiners a strong but likely temporary earnings and cash-flow tailwind; a potential US diesel export ban could cut export revenues and reshape refining margins.

stories.title: Deadly Blast Hits Major Indian Refinery as Fuel Markets Tighten
stories.summary: A fatal explosion damaged a processing unit at MRPL's Mangaluru refinery as Indian refiners run at unusually high rates amid tight diesel supplies.

stories.title: One killed, 12 injured in explosion at Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited
stories.summary: One person was killed and about a dozen injured in a blast at MRPL's Coker Hydro Treating Unit in Karnataka's Surathkal.

stories.title: US seeks to release another 40 million bbl from SPR despite low inventory levels
stories.summary: The US is seeking to release another 40 million bbl from the SPR despite already-low inventory levels, though it's unclear if companies will take the full offer.

stories.title: Week 39 - US DOE Inventory Recap
stories.summary: TACenergy's Week 39 recap covers the latest US DOE inventory data for gasoline, diesel and crude.

stories.title: EIA USA Demand Forecast Raised for 2026, Dropped for 2027
stories.summary: EIA raised its 2026 US total energy consumption forecast to 95.84 quadrillion Btu while trimming its 2027 projection to 96.77 quadrillion Btu.

stories.title: Oil Slides on Saudi Supply Relief
stories.summary: Crude prices fell as improving Saudi supply flows eased fears of further shortages, a backdrop factor for refining margins.

stories.title: USA Guts Auto Mileage Rules
stories.summary: The Trump administration finalized a significant weakening of federal fuel economy standards for automobiles, a move with long-run implications for gasoline demand.

stories.title: Clean Fuels applauds proposal to extend small agri-biodiesel producer credit by 3 years
stories.summary: Clean Fuels Alliance applauded a proposal to extend the small agri-biodiesel producer credit (20 cpg on first 15 million gallons for producers under 60 mgy) by three years.

stories.title: IRFA thanks bipartisan Senate effort to extend small biodiesel producer credit
stories.summary: The Iowa Renewable Fuels Association thanked a bipartisan Senate effort to extend the small biodiesel producer credit, which would provide certainty through 2029.

stories.title: Aether Fuels demonstrates Aurora™ equipment in fully integrated line producing on-spec synthetic aviation fuel
stories.summary: Aether Fuels demonstrated its Aurora equipment producing on-spec synthetic aviation fuel in a fully integrated line, validating its platform ahead of commercial deployment.

stories.title: Uniper Agrees Major SAF Offtake with Arcadia
stories.summary: Uniper agreed to buy 40,000 metric tons of electro-SAF from Arcadia eFuels' Project Endor in Denmark.

decks.title: 8-K exhibit d133400dex991.htm (filed 2026-09-29)
decks.analysis:
## Takeaways

- **Capital raise structure:** Delek US (NYSE: DK) intends to offer $400.0 million in convertible senior notes due November 1, 2031, with a 13-day, $60.0 million over-allotment option for initial purchasers (potential total: $460.0 million), sold via Rule 144A private placement to qualified institutional buyers.

- **Use of proceeds — deleveraging signal:** A portion funds capped call transactions (dilution offset); the remainder is earmarked for general corporate purposes, explicitly including **partial repayment of the Term Loan Credit Facility** (principal, accrued interest, fees/expenses) — a balance-sheet optimization move rather than growth capex, indicating no signaled change to refining/logistics investment plans.

- **No operational guidance changes:** The release contains no updates to throughput, utilization, capture rates, margins, renewable diesel/SAF economics, or RIN/LCFS exposure — this is purely a financing/liability-management transaction.

- **Refining footprint reference point:** Document reaffirms combined nameplate crude throughput capacity of **302,000 bpd** across Tyler and Big Spring (TX), El Dorado (AR), and Krotz Springs (LA) refineries — unchanged from prior disclosures, no capacity additions or idling mentioned.

- **Logistics ownership stake:** Delek and subsidiaries hold ~58.0% of Delek Logistics Partners, LP (NYSE: DKL) as of August 14, 2026, unchanged, with no new logistics asset drops or midstream capex commitments tied to this offering.

- **Redemption/conversion mechanics:** Notes are non-callable until November 6, 2029 (absent a cleanup redemption below 10% outstanding), and conversion terms (rate, interest) remain unset pending pricing — standard convertible structure with no embedded commodity-linked or fuels-market triggers.

## Market Signal

This is a balance-sheet management transaction — refinancing near-term term-loan debt into longer-dated convertible paper — with no indication of capacity changes, margin guidance, or renewable fuels strategy shifts, suggesting Delek's operational refining/logistics outlook remains steady while management prioritizes financial flexibility ahead of potential capex or macro refining-margin volatility.
